findings.reason: Web/Program.cs runs UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization and then UseCoreSyncHttpServer, with no fallback policy, RequireAuthorization or gating middleware, and RequireSyncReadWrite is never applied. A tokenless request therefore reaches the sync server, and the decision record admits this. I set it to high rather than critical because Entra mode isn't switched on for Web anywhere yet.
findings.claim: The CoreSync sync server accepts unauthenticated requests even with Auth:UseEntraId=true, so the sync channel is not protected.
findings.evidence: Program.cs calls app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); and then app.UseCoreSyncHttpServer(). It sets no FallbackPolicy, no RequireAuthorization, and no gating middleware, and the RequireSyncReadWrite policy (line 29) is never applied. UseAuthorization only enforces endpoint metadata, so a request to the CoreSync path with no Authorization header goes straight through to UseCoreSyncHttpServer. The builder's decision record admits this: 'does not reject unauthenticated requests (no RequireAuthorization() on CoreSync middleware endpoints)'.

members.evidence: With Auth:UseEntraId=true, a request without a Bearer token passes UseAuthentication(); UseAuthorization() has neither endpoint authorization metadata nor a fallback policy to enforce, and execution reaches UseCoreSyncHttpServer(). findings.reason: The middleware looks up the short names 'tid' and 'oid', and Program.cs never turns off MapInboundClaims. Whether these claims get renamed depends on Microsoft.Identity.Web/IdentityModel defaults that the repo doesn't show. TestJwtGenerator emits both claim forms, so the tests can't tell either way.
findings.claim: With real Entra tokens, default inbound claim mapping may rename tid/oid, so TenantId comes out null and UserId falls back to the mapped 'sub'.
findings.evidence: The middleware reads FindFirstValue("tid") ?? FindFirstValue("tenant_id") and FindFirstValue("oid") ?? FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier). AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi in Program.cs:34-35 doesn't turn off MapInboundClaims. When mapping is on, 'oid' becomes http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/objectidentifier and 'sub' becomes NameIdentifier, and Entra tokens carry no 'tenant_id'. The tests can't catch this: TestJwtGenerator adds both 'tid' and 'tenant_id', and both 'oid' and NameIdentifier with the same value, so API_ExtractsTenantContext passes whichever claim the middleware actually reads.

members.claim: With real Entra ID tokens, TenantId may come out null and UserId may be the token's 'sub' instead of 'oid'. This happens because the JWT handler's default inbound claim mapping renames 'tid'/'oid' to long URI claim types, so the new FindFirstValue("tid")/("oid") lookups find nothing.

findings.reason: Every MapGet/MapPost calls plain .RequireAuthorization() and none of the RequireScope policies is referenced. The decision record defers this on purpose. I lowered it to low: Microsoft.Identity.Web rejects tokens that carry no scp or roles claim by default, so the scope-less token case in the claim doesn't hold.
findings.claim: Scope policies are registered but no endpoint uses them, so any valid token for the API audience reaches every endpoint.

AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi doesn't check scopes unless a RequireScope policy or attribute is applied.
